\section[detener]{detener — to detain, to arrest; to stop}

\label{lesson:ES-C519-detener}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to hold up, then the Spanish for to flee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: detener}
\textbf{detener} — \textquotedblleft{}to detain, to arrest; to stop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La policía detuvo al ladrón en la estación.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The police arrested the thief at the station.}
\end{quote}

It changes like \emph{tener}: \emph{detuve}, \emph{detuvo}. \emph{Detenerse} is to stop: \emph{El coche se detuvo.}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{detener} is inherited from Latin \emph{dētinēre} 'to hold back' (EtymDB), built on \emph{dē-} and \emph{tenēre} 'to hold'. English \emph{detain} is the same Latin verb through French.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{detener}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{detener}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{detener}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to hold up, then the Spanish for to flee, then say \emph{detener} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does detener mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To detain, to arrest; to stop\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[arrestar]{arrestar — to arrest}

\label{lesson:ES-C519-arrestar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to flee, then the Spanish for to detain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: arrestar}
\textbf{arrestar} — \textquotedblleft{}to arrest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Arrestaron a tres personas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{They arrested three people.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Detener} is the more common word in the news; \emph{arrestar} is also used.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{arrestar} comes from spoken Latin \emph{*arrestāre} 'to make stop', built on \emph{ad} and \emph{restāre} 'to stay back, to remain' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arrestar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arrestar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{arrestar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to flee, then the Spanish for to detain, then say \emph{arrestar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does arrestar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To arrest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la detención]{la detención — the arrest}

\label{lesson:ES-C519-detencion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to detain, then the Spanish for to arrest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la detención}
\textbf{la detención} — \textquotedblleft{}the arrest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La detención fue rápida.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The arrest was quick.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{detención} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{dētentiō} 'a holding back' (EtymDB), from \emph{dētinēre}, built on \emph{tenēre} 'to hold'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la patrulla]{la patrulla — the patrol; the patrol car}

\label{lesson:ES-C519-patrulla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to arrest, then the Spanish for the arrest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la patrulla}
\textbf{la patrulla} — \textquotedblleft{}the patrol; the patrol car\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Una patrulla llegó en cinco minutos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A patrol car arrived in five minutes.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Estar de patrulla} — to be on patrol. \emph{Patrullar} is to patrol.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{patrulla} is built on \emph{patrullar} 'to patrol', which was borrowed from French \emph{patrouiller} (EtymDB). In Old French that verb meant 'to paddle, to paw about', and EtymDB builds it on \emph{patte} 'a paw'. The patrol tramped round on foot.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la patrulla}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la patrulla}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la patrulla}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to arrest, then the Spanish for the arrest, then say \emph{la patrulla} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la patrulla mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The patrol; the patrol car\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[perseguir]{perseguir — to chase, to pursue}

\label{lesson:ES-C519-perseguir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the arrest, then the Spanish for the patrol.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: perseguir}
\textbf{perseguir} — \textquotedblleft{}to chase, to pursue\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El perro persiguió al gato por la calle.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The dog chased the cat down the street.}
\end{quote}

It changes like \emph{seguir}: \emph{persigo}, \emph{persiguió}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{perseguir} is inherited from Latin \emph{persequī} 'to follow up, to pursue' (EtymDB), built on \emph{per} 'through' and \emph{sequī} 'to follow'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{perseguir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{perseguir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{perseguir}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the arrest, then the Spanish for the patrol, then say \emph{perseguir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

  \item the newsroom, the headline, the press, the correspondent, to publish
  \item the report, the reporter, to interview, to spread, to announce
  \item the rumour, the official statement, the statement, to declare, to confirm
  \item to assure, to correct, to reveal, to refute, the version
  \item the witness, to witness, to observe, to notice, the detail
  \item to steal, the robbery, the suspect, to hold up, to flee

The report? (\textbf{el reportaje}.) The reporter? (\textbf{el reportero}.) To interview? (\textbf{entrevistar}.) To spread? (\textbf{difundir}.) To announce? (\textbf{anunciar}.) The rumour? (\textbf{el rumor}.) The official statement? (\textbf{el comunicado}.) The statement? (\textbf{la declaración}.) To declare? (\textbf{declarar}.) To confirm? (\textbf{confirmar}.) To assure? (\textbf{asegurar}.) To correct? (\textbf{rectificar}.) To reveal? (\textbf{revelar}.) To refute? (\textbf{desmentir}.) The version? (\textbf{la versión}.) The witness? (\textbf{el testigo}.) To witness? (\textbf{presenciar}.) To observe? (\textbf{observar}.) To notice? (\textbf{percatarse}.) The detail? (\textbf{el detalle}.) To steal? (\textbf{robar}.) The robbery? (\textbf{el robo}.) The suspect? (\textbf{el sospechoso}.) To hold up? (\textbf{atracar}.) To flee? (\textbf{huir}.) To detain? (\textbf{detener}.) To arrest? (\textbf{arrestar}.) The arrest? (\textbf{la detención}.)
